title: Reading and Validating Input
introduction: User input begins as untrusted data and must be converted and checked before a program relies on it.
learningOutcomes: Handle boundaries and invalid values explicitly.

activities.question: What does parsing do?
options: Converts input text into a required type
activities.explanation: Parsing interprets text as a type such as a number; validation then checks whether the value is permitted.

activities.question: A successfully parsed age of -4 can still fail validation.
activities.explanation: The text can be a valid integer while the resulting value violates the program's rules.

activities.question: Order a safe input process.

items.text: Attempt to parse the required type

activities.explanation: Read, parse, validate and only then use the value.
